# Build a Jetpack

## Where is the options page?

The [player options page for Build a Jetpack](../player-options)
contains all the options you need to configure and export a config file.

## What is the goal of Build a Jetpack when randomized?

Reach the star high in the sky. This requires receiving three Jetpack items.

## Which items can be in another player's world?

Every upgrade (diving equipment, raft expansions, etc.) is shuffled into the item pool and can be found as an item.

## What is considered a location check in Build a Jetpack?

Buying upgrades sends location checks. If the option is enabled, selling unique types of fish for the first time will also send location checks.

## What does another world's item look like in Build a Jetpack?

Currently, items are not listed until they are sent. This may change in the future.

tutorials.text:
# Build a Jetpack Randomizer Setup Guide

## Required Software

- The Client folder from the release
- A web browser

### What is a YAML file and why do I need one?

See the guide on setting up a basic YAML at the Archipelago setup
guide: [Basic Multiworld Setup Guide](/tutorial/Archipelago/setup/en)

### Where do I get a YAML file?

You can customize your options by visiting the [Build a Jetpack Player Settings Page](../player-options)

## Joining a MultiWorld Game

### Launching the Build a Jetpack Client

The index.html file in the Client folder can be opened in any web browser, then submit the Hostname, Port, and Name for the connection

An example:
* Hostname: archipelago.gg
* Port: 38281
* Name: Player1

You will then see a `Connected` message showing that you have connected properly, and you can continue to play the game.

### Running the game

The game can be played before or after Connecting, but make sure if you are switching slots to reset the game so that your inventory and sent locations are not carried over into the new slot

![Banner](banner.png)

# Build a Jetpack - Archipelago Implementation

Source game from Aymeri: Build a Jetpack - https://www.lexaloffle.com/bbs/?pid=155669

License inhereted from Build a Jetpack - https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/

gpio-listener and webpage template - https://github.com/benwiley4000/pico8-gpio-listener

archipelago.js - https://www.npmjs.com/package/archipelago.js

gpio implementation, code reference, and web formatting from qwint: Air Delivery - https://github.com/qwint/ap-air-delivery

Some code reference from Amazia: MetroCUBEvania - https://github.com/ap-metrocubevania/ap-metrocubevania


A small game where you dive under the water and catch fish and materials, then use them to buy upgrades.

The goal is to get all three Jetpack items and reach the star in the sky.

The version of Build a Jetpack shipped with the AP integration has been modified to use the GPIO layer to communicate with archipelago.js, along with modifying the shop to send location checks.

Use the client zip to connect, or go here: https://www.chromanyan.page/buildajetpackap/



The AP version of the game features a sprite based on the Archipelago icon. The Archipelago icon is licensed as follows:

notes.text:
Improved the title screen

Added music shuffle, which can be toggled through the PICO-8 pause menu. As this is entirely client-side, a new random track will be picked every time the music changes. It has the following options:
- Vanilla: Music will not be shuffled
- Silent: Music will not play at all
- Random Simple (RNDSIMPLE): Only the underwater music will be randomized, and it will only pick underwater tracks + an unused music track
- Random Chaotic (RNDCHAOS): Shuffles all of the music in the game, including the raft ambience and low oxygen warning

The apworld has not changed from 0.3.0.
